text: 🇲🇽🌎 Mexico and Brazil trading technology, not selling out to foreign oil majors. "We’re very interested in the technology they’ve developed, and they’re interested in how we’ve improved fertilizer production." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on a joint Pemex–Petrobras proposal Sheinbaum floated Pemex and Petrobras jointly exploring the Gulf of Mexico. Petrobras cut deepwater exploration from ~10 years to as little as months; Mexico shares its fertilizer advances. South–South cooperation.

🇲🇽🏭 Mexico is building the largest solar plant in the Americas. "We’ll reach 1,000 MW of total capacity — the largest photovoltaic plant in the Americas. Total investment exceeds 1.4 billion dollars." — Emilia Calleja, CFE Director General Puerto Peñasco, Sonora — public and CFE-owned, not a private concession. The same plan includes the Oasis project in Baja California Sur: solar + batteries + green hydrogen.

🇲🇽🏭 By 2030 the State will supply 61% of Mexico’s electricity. "By 2030, the public sector will inject 61% of the nation’s electricity." — Luz Elena González, Secretary of Energy A reversal of the neoliberal model that handed generation to private firms. With the Expansion Plan, CFE and the State recover the majority of national power generation.

🇲🇽🛢️ The sun, the wind, geothermal — energies that guarantee sovereignty. "The first goal is to raise energy sovereignty. The sun, the wind, geothermal — these are available energies that guarantee sovereignty." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on the National Electric System Expansion Plan Mexico will add 32,475 MW of new capacity by 2030 — 70% renewable — with 739 billion pesos invested. Domestic sun and wind replace imported gas.

🇲🇽📈 <u>MEXICAN RETAIL CLIMBS 4.5% — INTERNAL DEMAND HOLDS THE LINE</u>

Retail sales rose 0.8% in April over March and 4.5% year-on-year, INEGI reported — the strongest monthly reading of the year, led by recreation, stationery and personal-use goods at 5.2%. El Economista notes the gains reached all 32 states. Domestic consumption keeps powering an economy the ratings agencies keep writing off.

🇲🇽🏛️ <u>HIDDEN FOR 1,000 YEARS: MAYA CITY "MINANBÉ" EMERGES FROM CALAKMUL</u>

A Mexican-Slovenian team working under INAH permits uncovered Minanbé — "no path" in Maya — deep in the Calakmul Biosphere Reserve: 15 hectares of plazas, palaces and a near-13-meter pyramid in exceptional condition, with readable glyphs and a 7th-century stela depicting a decapitation scene. The region held some 11 million people in the Late Classic. Lead archaeologist Iván Šprajc called reaching it "more complicated than to any other archaeological site."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SHEINBAUM WON'T TAKE THE BAIT: "I'M NOT FALLING FOR POLITICAL PROPAGANDA"</u>

As the opposition tries to manufacture a fight with Chihuahua governor Maru Campos over Rubén Rocha Moya, Sheinbaum shut it down from the National Palace: "Es propaganda política y no voy a caer en un asunto de propaganda." She called the noise politiquería and said everyone should just do their job. The destabilization playbook needs a reaction — she isn't giving one.

🇲🇽💵 <u>266 GLOBAL INVESTORS LINE UP AS MEXICO REFINANCES DEBT 3.3x OVERSUBSCRIBED</u>

Hacienda placed a $4.8 billion 11-year bond at 6.25% and reopened $1.5 billion more, using the proceeds to buy back $5.9 billion in short-term debt maturing 2027-2029 — without raising total debt one peso. Demand from 266 institutional investors ran 3.3 times the amount on offer. The "failed state" narrative, meet the bond market.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>AUDI WORKERS IN PUEBLA WIN 19.5% PACKAGE, KILL THE STRIKE THREAT</u>

Unionized workers at Audi's San José Chiapa plant approved a 19.5% global increase — 4.6% direct wage plus 14.9% in benefits — and a one-time 25,000-peso bonus, up 250% from the 7,000 pesos paid in 2024. 2,424 workers, 65% of those eligible, voted yes through the night of June 23. Independent union, real bargaining — the labor reform working exactly as intended.

🇲🇽⚡ <u>MEXICO BETS 739 BILLION PESOS ON PUBLIC, RENEWABLE POWER</u>

Sheinbaum unveiled a plan to add 32,475 MW to the national grid by 2030 — 70% of the new capacity renewable, with the CFE building 79% of it and the State keeping ownership of every asset. Renewables climb from 24% to 38% of the mix, and the 1,000 MW Puerto Peñasco solar park is set to be the largest in the Americas. Built and owned by the public utility neoliberalism spent decades trying to dismantle.
